back: Writing a new text for a given audience and purpose using ideas selected from one or two reading texts.
Judging ideas: how convincing, reliable, practical or complete they are, with reasons.
Taking an idea further: consequences, links or application to the audience.
Combining related ideas from different texts or parts of a text into one point.
Read the task → annotate the texts (for/against) → plan by idea → write in role, in your own words, evaluating.
The most convincing argument is…; While it is true that…, this ignores…; no evidence is given; Both writers agree that…
Copying long phrases from the text; it earns little credit. Use your own words.

front: Questions to ask of a text
back: Is it supported? Fact or opinion? Practical? Is anything missing? Do the texts agree?
